title: Offers and pricing
purpose: When someone wants to run a discount, change a price, build a bundle or set a threshold, open Offers and pricing to see what it will do to gross profit per order before it goes live, and what it did after.
fires: The discount calendar copied from last year, the "let's do 20 percent off" reflex, the offer math done in a spreadsheet after the sale, and the app vendor's word that their upsell works.
not_for: A brand whose prices are set by retailers under wholesale terms, or a store that sells mostly by subscription; the subscription version comes later.

jobs.job: When someone on the team or at the agency wants to run a discount this week, show me what it costs in gross profit and how many extra orders it needs to pay back, before it runs, so I do not give away the month's profit
jobs.circumstance: Thursday, the agency proposes 25 percent off this weekend "to hit the month", and no one has done the math

progress.functional: know gross profit per order after the discount, the extra orders needed to break even, and whether it crosses my floor
progress.emotional: stop the sinking feeling after a sale that sold a lot and made nothing
progress.social: say yes or no to the agency with numbers, not mood

jobs.hire_today: a spreadsheet after the sale, the agency's promise, or gut feel
jobs.fire: the after-the-fact spreadsheet and the "let's just try it" call

forces.push: a wrong sale gives away a month of profit in a weekend
forces.pull: the cost and the break-even lift, shown before I approve
forces.habit: we always run a weekend sale when the month is slow
forces.anxiety: what if the model is too careful and we miss sales we needed

watch.metric: gross profit per order after discount, per offer, against the owner's floor
watch.source: Shopify orders and discounts, product costs in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a 25 percent sale sold 900 orders and made $2,100 less than a normal weekend. After: the math shows it needs 60 percent more orders, so a gift offer runs instead and adds $3,400.
jobs.not_for: a store with no product costs entered; the answer would be a guess

jobs.job: When sales only come during promotions, tell me how much of our revenue now depends on a discount and how fast that grew, so I stop training buyers to wait for the next sale
jobs.circumstance: Full-price weeks are dead, and buyers email asking when the next sale is

progress.functional: know the share of revenue sold at a discount over 12 months
progress.emotional: stop the dread of full-price weeks
progress.social: show the team why we are cutting back on sales

jobs.hire_today: gut feel, or the discount line in the bookkeeper's report

forces.push: margin falls every quarter
forces.pull: the trend in one line, with its cost
forces.habit: run a sale when the month is slow
forces.anxiety: what if revenue drops when we pull back

watch.metric: share of revenue sold at a discount, 90 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 58 percent of revenue is sold at a discount, up from 30. After: 40 percent in 6 months, with gross margin up 5 points.
jobs.not_for: an outlet or clearance store where discounting is the model

jobs.job: When Black Friday or another big sale is 8 weeks out, plan the offer so the sale adds profit and does not just pull orders forward, so the season lifts the year
jobs.circumstance: September, the Black Friday plan is due, and last year's 30 percent off sold a lot while December was dead

progress.functional: know the profit of the sale plus the 30 days after, against no sale
progress.social: give the team a plan with a profit goal, not an order goal

jobs.hire_today: last year's plan, or the agency's plan

forces.push: the season is a big share of the year
forces.pull: an offer judged on profit before the season starts
forces.habit: a bigger discount than last year
forces.anxiety: what if we sell less than rivals who go deeper

watch.metric: gross profit during the sale plus the 30 days after, against the same period with no sale

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a sale made $40k and then December lost $25k. After: a gift offer makes $52k with no December dip.
jobs.not_for: a brand that does not take part in seasonal sales

jobs.job: When a tariff, freight or supplier cost rise lands, help me choose between raising price, changing the pack or absorbing it, so margin holds without losing buyers
jobs.circumstance: Landed cost is up 12 percent after a duty change, and 3 options are on the table

progress.functional: know the profit and buyer effect of each option
progress.emotional: make a hard call without panic
progress.social: explain the choice to the team and to retail partners

jobs.hire_today: the bookkeeper, gut feel, or waiting

forces.push: every week of waiting costs margin
forces.pull: 3 options costed side by side
forces.habit: absorb it and hope costs fall
forces.anxiety: what if we choose wrong and lose buyers

watch.metric: gross margin per unit on the products hit, before and after the change, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a 12 percent rise was absorbed and margin fell 5 points. After: a 6 percent price rise and a pack change hold margin.
jobs.not_for: a store with flat costs and no price pressure

jobs.job: When shipping costs eat margin on small orders, set the free shipping line where it pays for itself and lifts order size, so we stop paying to ship every small order
jobs.circumstance: Free shipping over $50, a pile of orders at $52, and carriers raised rates in January

progress.functional: know the line that earns the most gross profit per order, from our own order sizes and shipping costs
progress.emotional: stop wondering if free shipping is a gift or a trap

jobs.hire_today: copying rivals' line, or a calculator filled in by hand once
jobs.fire: the line set years ago and never checked

forces.push: shipping is a large cost on small orders
forces.pull: a line set from our own orders, rechecked when costs move
forces.anxiety: what if a higher line drops conversion

jobs.little_hire: each quarter, and when carrier rates or order size change

watch.metric: share of orders just over the line, and shipping cost per order, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the line is $50 and shipping is 14 percent of order value. After: the line is $65, order size is up $8 and shipping is 10 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store where every order is well above any sensible line

jobs.job: When the product is good but shoppers hesitate, build the offer around their biggest doubt, at a price that still makes money, so more people buy without a deeper discount
jobs.circumstance: The page converts at 1.6 percent, buyers doubt fit and wear, and the team wants 20 percent off

progress.functional: know the top doubt, and an offer part that removes it, costed
progress.emotional: stop reaching for discounts as the only lever
progress.social: bring the team a better answer than "cut price"

jobs.hire_today: the agency's offer ideas, or a discount
jobs.fire: the discount as the default fix

forces.push: discounts cost margin on every order
forces.pull: an offer that removes the doubt, priced
forces.anxiety: what if the doubt we pick is the wrong one

jobs.little_hire: at each offer review and product launch

watch.metric: product page conversion rate with the new offer, 14 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 20 percent off is planned. After: a free fit exchange runs instead, conversion rises 15 percent and no discount is needed.
jobs.not_for: a store where the problem is traffic, not doubt on the page

jobs.job: When order size is stuck, build bundles and multi-packs that raise it without giving away margin, so each order earns more
jobs.circumstance: Most orders are 1 item at $14, and the 3-pack and 6-pack exist with no clear reason to pick them

progress.functional: know units per order and gross profit per order for each pack option

jobs.hire_today: a merchandiser, or copying rival packs

forces.push: small orders barely cover shipping and ads
forces.pull: packs priced so every tier clears the margin floor
forces.anxiety: what if the pack eats single sales and adds nothing

watch.metric: units per order and gross profit per order, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1.3 units per order. After: 1.8, with gross profit per order up $6.
jobs.not_for: a high-ticket single item nobody buys 2 of

jobs.job: When a discount code leaks to coupon sites and browser extensions, find it and shut it, so we stop giving discounts to buyers who were already at checkout
jobs.circumstance: A creator's code shows up on coupon sites, and 20 percent of orders now use it

progress.functional: know which codes are used by people outside their intended audience
progress.emotional: stop the feeling of being robbed at checkout

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. Codes are made and forgotten, and nobody tracks where they spread

forces.push: leaked codes discount buyers who would have paid full price
forces.pull: leaks found, with the cost
forces.habit: make a code for every partner
forces.anxiety: what if shutting a code upsets a partner

watch.metric: discount spend on codes used outside their intended audience, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $4,800 a month goes on a leaked creator code. After: the code is limited, and the cost is $600.
jobs.not_for: a store with no discount codes

jobs.job: When anyone on the team or at the agency can make a discount code, set rules on how deep, how often and for whom, so no one gives away margin without my say
jobs.circumstance: 47 active codes, and 5 were made by the agency without asking

progress.functional: know the active codes, who made them and what they cost
progress.emotional: stop the feeling of losing control
progress.social: set clear rules the team and agency follow

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. Codes are made in Shopify by anyone with access, because no one set a rule

forces.push: every stray code costs margin
forces.pull: rules, plus a list of what is live
forces.habit: whoever needs a code makes one
forces.anxiety: what if the rules slow down a real chance to sell

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and when a code is made

watch.metric: active codes outside the discount rules, and their cost, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 47 codes, 12 outside any rule, costing $5k a month. After: 15 codes, all within the rules.
jobs.not_for: a founder who makes every code personally

jobs.job: When costs have risen and margin is thin, find out if we can charge more without losing buyers, so we raise profit per order instead of cutting costs to the bone
jobs.circumstance: The price has not changed in 3 years, and costs are up 18 percent

progress.functional: know conversion and gross profit per visitor at a new price
progress.emotional: get past the fear of raising prices

jobs.hire_today: gut feel, or rival prices

forces.push: margin shrinks every year
forces.pull: a small test judged on profit per visitor
forces.anxiety: what if buyers leave and do not come back

watch.metric: conversion rate and gross profit per visitor at the new price, 14 to 28 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $14. After: $16, conversion down 3 percent and gross profit per visitor up 11 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store that raised prices in the last 6 months

jobs.job: When an offer or price changes, tell me and the media buyer the new most we can pay per purchase, so ads are not judged against yesterday's target
jobs.circumstance: A bundle launched, order value is up $15, and the buyer still cuts ads above the old target

progress.functional: know the break-even cost per purchase at the current offer
progress.social: give the media buyer a clear new target

jobs.hire_today: the media buyer's old target, or a spreadsheet
jobs.fire: the target set once a year

forces.push: wrong targets kill good ads or keep bad ones
forces.pull: a target that updates with the offer
forces.anxiety: what if the new target lets spend run too loose

jobs.little_hire: at every offer or price change

watch.metric: break-even cost per purchase at the current offer
watch.source: Shopify orders, product costs in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the target is $30 after the bundle raised break-even to $41. After: the target is reset in a day and 2 good ad sets are kept.
jobs.not_for: a store that runs no paid ads

jobs.job: When buyers fear the product will not work or fit, offer a guarantee that removes the risk without breaking margin if claims run high, so more people try us
jobs.circumstance: A 30 day return policy, rivals offer longer, and the founder fears abuse

progress.functional: know the claim rate, the cost per claim and the lift in sales

jobs.hire_today: copying a rival's policy, or gut feel
jobs.fire: the policy set once, out of fear

forces.pull: a guarantee costed before launch
forces.habit: keep it short to be safe
forces.anxiety: what if claims run 3 times higher than planned

watch.metric: guarantee claims as a share of covered orders, 60 day, against plan

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 30 days and 1.7 percent conversion. After: 1 year, claims at 3 percent and conversion at 2.0.
jobs.not_for: a product that cannot be resold or reused once opened, where a long guarantee is too costly

jobs.job: When loyal customers get the same discount as new ones, set different offers for each, so we stop paying buyers who would have come back anyway
jobs.circumstance: Every email carries 15 percent off, and repeat buyers use it on orders they would place anyway

watch.metric: discount spend per returning customer order, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $6 of discount per returning order. After: $2, with a gift perk instead, and the repeat rate holds.

jobs.job: When a sale ends, tell me what it really earned against a normal week, counting the dip after, so I know whether to run it again
jobs.circumstance: Monday after a sale, and the team is celebrating the order count

progress.functional: know the sale's real gross profit lift
progress.emotional: know if the celebration is earned

jobs.hire_today: the order count, or the agency's report

forces.push: bad sales get repeated
forces.pull: a fair read, with the dip counted
forces.anxiety: what if the read looks bad for a sale I pushed

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: "best weekend ever". After: +$4k once the dip is counted, not +$30k.

jobs.job: When every new visitor gets 15 percent off for their email, tell me whether that pop-up offer pays for itself after the discount, so we stop paying buyers who would have bought anyway
jobs.circumstance: Every new visitor gets 15 percent off for their email, and 70 percent of first orders use the welcome code

jobs.hire_today: an email freelancer, or the pop-up app's report

forces.push: the code quietly discounts most first orders
forces.pull: the offer judged on profit
forces.anxiety: what if list growth drops without the code

watch.metric: first-order gross profit from pop-up signups, after the discount, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 15 percent off costs $22k a quarter. After: a gift replaces it, list growth holds and $12k is saved.
jobs.not_for: a store with no email pop-up

jobs.job: When a rival runs a big sale, help me answer without matching their price, so we keep our buyers and our margin

forces.push: matching kills margin
forces.pull: a non-price answer, costed

jobs.little_hire: whenever a rival runs a sale

watch.metric: our conversion rate and gross profit in rival sale weeks, against normal weeks

jobs.job: When an ad promises one offer and the page, cart or email shows another, catch it before buyers do, so they do not feel tricked at checkout

jobs.hire_today: spot checks by the agency or the founder

forces.push: mismatches kill checkout and trust
forces.pull: mismatches caught early
forces.anxiety: what if checks miss a channel

watch.metric: checkout completion rate on ad traffic, 7 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a mismatch ran for 4 days. After: it is caught before launch.
jobs.not_for: a store with one evergreen offer that never changes

jobs.job: When a new product is about to launch, set its price from its full cost, the rival range and what buyers said they would pay, so we launch at a price that sells and makes money
jobs.circumstance: Launch in 4 weeks, cost known, and 3 price ideas on the table

progress.functional: know the price that clears our margin floor and sits in the buyers' range
progress.social: agree the price with the team fast

jobs.hire_today: cost times 3, matching a rival, or gut feel

forces.push: a wrong launch price is hard to fix later
forces.pull: one price, with the reasons

watch.metric: launch gross margin per unit and conversion in the first 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: priced at cost times 3, which is $12. After: $16 from buyer and rival data, with conversion on plan.

jobs.job: When stock is sitting and cash is tight, clear slow items with an offer that frees cash without cheapening the best sellers, so we get cash back without hurting the brand
jobs.circumstance: $40k in last season's colors, with 200 days of stock

progress.functional: know which slow items to clear, the offer, and the cash it frees
progress.emotional: stop looking at the dead stock

jobs.hire_today: a sitewide sale, or a liquidator
jobs.fire: sitewide sales that also cut best sellers

forces.anxiety: what if clearance buyers never pay full price again

watch.metric: units of stock older than 180 days sold, and cash recovered, 30 day

jobs.job: When an upsell app shows lots of clicks, tell me whether it adds profit against buyers who did not see it, so I stop paying for an app that only moves sales around

forces.pull: a fair read against a held-out group
forces.anxiety: what if pulling the app loses real profit

watch.metric: gross profit added per order by upsells, against a group that did not see them, 30 day

jobs.not_for: a store with no upsell or cross-sell apps

jobs.job: When I want to lift order size, use a free gift that moves buyers to the tier we want at a cost lower than a discount, so order size rises and margin holds

jobs.hire_today: gut feel, or copying a rival
jobs.fire: the cash discount as the only lever

forces.push: discounts cost more than gifts
forces.pull: a gift tier, costed
forces.anxiety: what if buyers do not value the gift

watch.metric: share of orders on the gift tier, and gift cost as a share of order value, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 20 percent off. After: a gift at $65, order size up $11 and the gift costing 4 percent of the order.
jobs.not_for: a luxury brand where a free gift cheapens the product

jobs.job: When a buyer wants to return, offer store credit or an exchange before a refund where they will take it, so we keep the sale and the customer
jobs.circumstance: 12 percent returns, and almost all are refunded

progress.functional: know the share of returns kept as credit or exchange

jobs.hire_today: the support lead, or the returns app defaults

forces.push: refunds lose the sale
forces.pull: credit and exchange shown first
forces.anxiety: what if buyers feel trapped and leave angry

watch.metric: share of returns taken as store credit or exchange, 30 day

jobs.job: When we plan a new offer, show me what similar offers earned before, so we do not repeat a loser or forget a winner

progress.functional: know past offers and their profit results

jobs.job: When a "was" price or a "save 50 percent" line goes on the site, check we really sold at that price, so we do not break pricing rules or buyers' trust

jobs.hire_today: the loyalty app's report

forces.push: 5 percent of revenue is real money
forces.pull: a fair comparison
forces.habit: keep it because buyers expect it
forces.anxiety: what if cutting it angers the best buyers

watch.metric: repeat purchase rate at 180 days, members against similar non-members

drives.metric: gross profit per customer at 180 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: points cost $60k a year. After: members rebuy 4 points more, worth $35k, so the program is cut back to the top tier.
jobs.not_for: a store with no loyalty program

jobs.job: When bigger orders stall at checkout, offer pay-in-parts where it lifts sales and check the fee is worth it, so large baskets close
jobs.circumstance: Carts over $100 are abandoned more often

progress.functional: know conversion on big orders with pay-in-parts shown, and the fee

jobs.hire_today: the app vendor's claims

forces.push: big carts lost
forces.pull: the lift and the fee side by side
forces.anxiety: what if the fee eats the gain

watch.metric: conversion rate on orders over $100 with pay-in-parts shown, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no read. After: +6 percent on big carts against a 5 percent fee, so it is kept for orders over $100 only.
jobs.not_for: a store where most orders are under $50
